evals.prompt: About 15% of my survey respondents skipped the income question and some other items. How should I handle the missing data before modeling?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-missing-data: first requires an explicit MCAR/MAR/MNAR mechanism statement, then prescribes multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) with Rubin's-rules pooling — not mean imputation or listwise deletion.

assertions.value: Demands a missingness mechanism and prescribes multiple imputation with Rubin's-rules pooling over single imputation.

evals.prompt: Can I just fill the missing values with the column mean and run my regression?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-missing-data: warns that mean/single imputation treats imputed values as observed and understates standard errors, and routes to multiple imputation with pooling instead.

assertions.value: Rejects mean/single imputation as biasing standard errors and prescribes multiple imputation.

evals.prompt: I created 20 imputed datasets and ran my model on each. How do I combine the results?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-missing-data: applies Rubin's rules to pool the estimates (mean) and standard errors (within + between variance), e.g. mice::pool or statsmodels MICE, and reports the fraction of missing information.

evals.prompt: My dataset is complete with no missing values — just run the regression and give me the coefficients.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-statistical-analysis. With complete data there is no missingness to handle.

evals.prompt: I'm fitting a structural equation model and want to use FIML to handle missing data inside the SEM.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-sem-psychometrics. FIML inside a latent-variable model is fit by the psychometrics skill.
